question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}6{e}^{-6x},\, & x\ge 0 \\ 0,\, & x<0\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<0 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.

Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14122710/assets/9bab7992e89938dad8c9fafb358532958e1588f2b80b6cb05f60c2e6c8a20fb7.svg)

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x \geq 0,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14122710/assets/d34196e7c9b9112e71a297c2b970c9f6318b225755f74b955ddd44c9566a7b82.svg)

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & =-{e}^{-t}{|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-{e}^{-x}+1 \\  & =1-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14122710/assets/a09009b1a1ee17d45d31493194c3bf48c0835c8f0a944d39a232676bb8f59491.svg)
